Portion Air fryer Oven reheat Party wings, flats and drumettes 375°F / 190°C · 4 min 375°F / 190°C · 8 min Standard split wings 375°F / 190°C · 5 min 375°F / 190°C · 10 min Jumbo wings 375°F / 190°C · 7 min 375°F / 190°C · 14 min Why the sauce burns before the wing is hot Most wing sauces are built on sugar: honey, brown sugar, ketchup, barbecue sauce or sweet chilli. Sugar starts to caramelise at a much lower temperature than it takes to heat a cold wing to the bone, and in an air fryer the sauce sits on the outside, right in the hot airflow. So the glaze goes dark, then bitter and black, while the meat inside is still cool. Buffalo sauce has less sugar but separates, leaving a puddle of butter. The fix is to reheat the wing, not the sauce. Scrape or wipe off thick glaze, reheat the wings close to plain, and toss them in fresh or warmed sauce at the end. Dry-rubbed wings can go straight in. Worked example: a takeaway box of wings Eight leftover barbecue wings with the thickest sauce wiped off. Preheat 4 minutes, spread them in a single layer and heat at 375°F for 5 minutes, shaking once. Party-size flats and drumettes need about 4 minutes and jumbo wings about 7. Toss in warm sauce and return for a minute to set it. In a conventional oven, the same wings reheat at 375°F for around 10 minutes. How to tell they are ready Check the meatiest drumette next to the bone: USDA guidance is 165°F (74°C) for reheated leftovers. The skin should be crisp and sizzling, and any sauce left on should be bubbling, not black. Dark edges with a cool middle mean too much sauce stayed on. Before they go in Keep any sauce from the box to warm separately. Wipe sticky wings with a paper towel; a thin film is fine. Separate wings that have stuck together so air reaches every side. No oil is needed. Wings that were sauced the night before have soaked some of it into the skin, so they will never be quite as crisp as dry-rubbed ones; the short reheat and fresh sauce get them close. Cook them in a single layer, in two rounds if needed. About 5 minutes at 375°F for standard wings, shaken once. Party wings take around 4 minutes and jumbo wings around 7. Why do my reheated wings burn? The sugar in the sauce caramelises long before the meat is hot. Wipe off thick sauce first and add fresh sauce at the end. Can I reheat buffalo wings in the air fryer? Yes. Buffalo sauce splits when reheated, so reheat the wings plain and toss them in warm sauce afterwards. What temperature should reheated wings reach? 165°F (74°C) next to the bone, which is USDA guidance for any reheated leftovers. How do I reheat wings in the oven? On a rack over a tray at 375°F for around 10 minutes, then toss in sauce.
